summary_rationale: Jyoti CNC Automation possesses a genuine engineering franchise: a top-three domestic market position (~8-10% overall share, leading domestic 5-axis CNC builder), vertical integration via its Rajkot captive foundry and 16,000-machine capacity expansion, and a ₹5,082 Cr order book as of September 2026 anchored in aerospace, defence, automotive, and EMS. Revenue more than tripled from ₹532 Cr (FY21) to ₹2,093 Cr (FY26) with OPM expanding to 25% and ROCE at 21.3%. However, cash-conversion and balance-sheet forensics prevent a COMPOUNDER_PASS: the business posted four consecutive net losses across FY20-FY23, generated -₹847 Cr in cumulative Free Cash Flow over FY24-FY26 (CFO/EBITDA conversion of 1%, -4%, and 34%), carries extreme 453-day inventory and 234-day working capital cycles, and has tripled borrowings back from ₹304 Cr post-IPO (Mar 2024) to ₹946 Cr (Sep 2026). Compounding this, French subsidiary Huron Graffenstaden faces an active April 2026 dual-use export-control investigation with ~€4M frozen and posted a ~₹43 Cr net loss in Q2 FY27.
